page.text: When your media already matches the call, NTgCalls sends it as it is, without decoding and encoding it again. You get the original quality and a fraction of the CPU.

list.item: Opus audio, from Ogg, WebM, MKA or YouTube
H264 Baseline, Main or High without B-frames, VP8, VP9 or AV1, in the codec and size of the call
MP3, AAC, FLAC, Vorbis and WAV audio
H264 with B-frames, like most phone videos and downloads, and 10-bit, 4:2:2, 4:4:4 or interlaced H264, which many phones can't decode
A video codec or size different from the call, or above the size and frame rate of your VideoParameters
Recording several participants, or to .mp4, .m4a, .wav or .flac

page.text: Re-encoding is automatic, so everything still plays. It only costs more CPU.
Convert it once, with Opus audio and H264 without B-frames at the size of your VideoParameters:
Audio sent as it is keeps the bitrate of the file and doesn't follow the connection, while re-encoded audio adapts to it. Pick what suits your server:

list.item: Fixed: on a stable, fast connection, use Opus files encoded at the bitrate you want. They are sent as they are, with constant quality.
Adaptive: on an unstable connection, let NTgCalls encode the audio. It lowers the bitrate when the bandwidth drops and adds error correction when packets get lost.

page.text: To always re-encode an Opus source, set a bitrate in AudioParameters lower than the one of the file. Passthrough also switches to re-encoding on its own when the channels don't match.
Before playing, get_media_info() tells whether a file can be sent as it is:
page.syntax-highlight:
from ntgcalls import NTgCalls, StreamMode
info = NTgCalls.get_media_info('song.webm', StreamMode.CAPTURE) print(info.audio.passthrough)
page.text: While playing, enable the ntgcalls logger to see whether each stream is forwarded or re-encoded, and why:
page.syntax-highlight: INFO:ntgcalls:libav_demuxer.cpp:134 Sending the Opus audio without re-encoding it INFO:ntgcalls:passthrough_video_encoder.cpp:87 Forwarding the encoded H264 video without re-encoding it INFO:ntgcalls:passthrough_video_encoder.cpp:102 Re-encoding the video, the source uses B-frames
page.text: Lines starting with Sending or Forwarding mean passthrough. Re-encoding lasts for the whole file and says why at the end, while Encoding the video until the next usable source keyframe lasts only a moment, after a bandwidth drop or a keyframe request.
